subject: Request: tenant-level isolation toggle + rollback plan for Orion Health pilot
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@orionhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Pillai <raj.pillai@orionhealth.com>, procurement@orionhealth.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant-level isolation toggle for pilot (timing & rollback)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move the Orion Health pilot into a limited production slice. Two ask items from our infra and procurement teams that are blocking the kickoff: 

1) We need a tenant-level isolation toggle (ability to opt a tenant into an isolated cache/worker path) for data separation during the pilot. This is temporary — we want a configuration flag per-tenant that can be enabled/disabled without a model rollout.

2) A clear rollback and safe-launch plan. Procurement requires a brief technical runbook for how Redwood would mute/rollback the change if behavior/regressions appear (including a kill-switch).

Attached is a short requirements doc and the redlined SLA page we expect to finalize this week. Can you confirm Redwood can commit to a timeline for an MVE (minimum viable enable) and the rollback-runbook? Our commercial team has a go-live target of May 31, but procurement needs the tech confirmation to sign.

Appreciate a quick confirmation — happy to hop on a 30m call if helpful.

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Program Manager, Integrations
Orion Health

Team — forwarding Orion's asks. Short version: this is a near-term revenue gate for a 6-figure pilot; they need a tenant toggle and a documented rollback/kill-switch. Go-live target May 31.

Context and constraints:
- This should be implemented as a config toggle, not a model change. They want to flip a per-tenant flag to route traffic to an isolated cache/worker path.
- Security wants the change to be limited in scope for the pilot and reversible quickly.
- Procurement will not sign unless we provide a short rollback runbook and a timeline for MVE.

Marissa (sales) ask: can Product + Eng evaluate feasibility and give a 5-business-day MVE estimate? If feasible, we should prioritize as a deal-driven exception and scope an MVE that includes tests and a short QA checklist.

Next steps proposed:
1) Product to propose MVE scope and minimal safe-launch checklist.
2) Eng to confirm schematic (worker routing + cache isolation) and list any capacity/infra needs.
3) Draft rollback runbook and attach to procurement doc.

Please reply with feasibility + ownership by EOD Tuesday so I can update Orion procurement.

—Marissa
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Tenant-level isolation toggle for pilot (timing & rollback)

Thanks Marissa — quick triage from Product side after a first-pass with Eng.

Feasibility: plausible with caveats. Two implementation approaches:

A) Config flag + routing to dedicated worker pool and isolated KV/cache namespace. Pros: minimal model changes, quick toggle. Cons: requires separate cache namespace semantics or prefixing keys per-tenant and careful KV cache invalidation rules.

B) Traffic tagging + soft isolation (same worker pool, request-level tenant isolation). Pros: faster to ship, lower infra footprint. Cons: weaker isolation guarantees (shared cache), may not satisfy their procurement/SOC expectations.

For procurement and security, they appear to expect stronger isolation — so we should aim for approach A for the pilot. Preliminary MVE scope (what we can deliver quickly):
- Tenant config flag stored in account metadata (UI/API).
- Router change to inspect tenant flag and route to an isolated pool.
- Per-tenant cache prefixing and KV namespace separation for the pilot tenants.
- Kill-switch: feature gate to force all traffic back to default pool + cache flush for the tenant.
- Basic smoke tests and per-tenant latency/cost metrics dashboard widgets.

Estimated timeline (MVE): 3 weeks of focused work (2 engineers full-time + 1 part-time QA/product) to ship a skeleton MVE with manual runbook. If we do a smaller-scope B approach, could be 4-6 business days.

Requirements from Sales/CS: list of pilot tenant IDs, expected QPS for pilot, and acceptance criteria (isolation definition). Also need Security sign-off on KV namespace separation.

I've attached a draft design doc with the routing diagram and rollback steps (tenant-isolation-draft-design.md). Dev — can you confirm infra needs (extra worker nodes, cache partitions) and whether the kill-switch requires an automated orchestration change or can be a manual operator step?

—David
Product Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachment: tenant-isolation-draft-design.md

Subject: Re: Tenant-level isolation toggle for pilot (timing & rollback)

Thanks David — good breakdown and clear tradeoffs. A few directives to keep this deal moving: 

1) Prioritize plan A (isolated pool + per-tenant namespace) for the Orion pilot. The customer will not sign for approach B. Treat this as a deal-driven exception and allocate capacity accordingly.

2) Deliverables and deadlines:
- MVE scope document (one pager) outlining exactly what will be delivered for May 31 target — due by EOD May 24.
- A short rollback-runbook that can be handed to Orion procurement (1-2 pages) — due by EOD May 24.
- Capacity / infra ask: Dev to provide a short list of infra items and estimated cost impact by EOD May 21.

3) QA and safety gates: include a smoke-test checklist (latency, error-rate, cache correctness) and include a manual kill-switch that can be invoked by the on-call operator; automation is not required for MVE but should be scoped for post-MVE.

4) Communication: Marissa, please tell Orion procurement we will provide the MVE scope + runbook by May 24 and a firm delivery cadence for May 31. Monica, please prep a brief customer-facing note describing what the pilot isolation covers and the limitations.

I'll approve the deal exception for the resources required (assume two FTEs) pending the scope doc and infra ask. If Product/Eng feel this is unachievable within these windows, escalate to me immediately.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Enterprise Sales (acting)
Redwood Inference
